title: Salmon and Tuna Poke Bowls
summary: Lightly cured salmon and ahi tuna over warm short-grain rice with charred edamame, quick-pickled carrots, homemade fried shallots, radish, avocado and green onion, with ponzu and a numbing spicy mayo on the side.
notes: Video: 'The Healthiest Poke Bowls at Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/easy-healthy-homemade-poke-bowls-recipe (serves 4, prep 30 min, cook 45 min). The video states the fish, marinade, rice, pickle, shallots, edamame and both sauces. From the written recipe, where the captions are garbled or give a range: 1/2 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp sesame oil in the marinade, 2 avocados (video: two to three), 4-5 green onions (we use 4). Radishes: the video says four to five, we use 4. Edamame salt (1/2 tsp kosher) is our estimate. Not counted: the pickling liquid, the garlic cloves left whole in the marinade, the frying oil for the shallots (absorption unknown, so fat is understated), and both sauces, which are served on the side (the spicy mayo alone is about 1,300 kcal for the batch if all of it is eaten). Raw fish: sushi-grade only. Shallot weight (4 medium, about 160 g) is our estimate; USDA gives no per-shallot weight. Mirin and gochujang use branded records.

steps.text: Cut the salmon and tuna into 1/2-inch cubes with single clean strokes, keeping the fish cold.
Gently fold the fish with the salt, sugar, mirin, sesame oil, white shoyu and the crushed whole garlic. Cover and refrigerate while you prep the rest.

Rinse the short-grain rice about three times until the water runs mostly clear, level it, add an equal volume of water and cook in a rice cooker. Fluff as soon as it's done and let it cool about 10 minutes.
Whisk the vinegar, water, salt and sugar until dissolved. Julienne the carrots and toss them in the liquid.

Slice the shallots just under 1/4 inch. Put them in a pot of cold neutral oil (no more than half full), heat over medium and stir constantly for 5-8 minutes, until they stop bubbling and are lightly golden. Drain on paper towels and salt them while hot; they crisp as they cool.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high until nearly smoking. Add the edamame, salt, and sear undisturbed 2-3 minutes, then toss until hot through. Finish with lemon juice.
Ponzu (optional): whisk the soy sauce, yuzu juice, mirin and rice vinegar; steep with kombu and katsuobushi 10-15 minutes or overnight, then strain.
Spicy mayo: whisk the Kewpie, Sriracha, gochujang, ground Sichuan pepper, rice vinegar, soy sauce, and a pinch each of sugar and salt.
Slice the green onions into thin threads and crisp them in ice water; dry well. Slice the radishes paper-thin and the avocados.
Build each bowl: rice, marinated fish, avocado, edamame, drained carrots, radish, fried shallots, green onion and furikake. Serve the sauces on the side.
